title: NIDCD says a baby's first communication is learning that a cry brings care
summary: NIDCD says the first signs of communication come when an infant learns that a cry brings food, comfort, and companionship.
body: The NIDCD milestone page says the first signs of communication occur when an infant learns that a cry will bring food, comfort, and companionship. It also says newborns begin to recognize important sounds, such as the voice of their mother or primary caretaker. The cry sentence is about what the cry does in care, not about the CDC 2-month line on sounds other than crying. The page does not say crying is a language with grammar. It is the institute's description of an early step.

sources.title: Speech and Language Developmental Milestones
sources.author: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Opened 2026-11-26. The page prints NIH Publication No. 00-4781, September 2010, and no later review date. Supports the sentence that the first signs of communication occur when an infant learns that a cry will bring food, comfort, and companionship.
